Suicide mortality in Korea, 2010–2021: a nationwide spatiotemporal analysis

Keywords: suicide mortality, spatiotemporal analysis, mental health facilities, Bayesian hierarchical model, INLA, BYM, South Korea

Key findings
  • 166,795 suicide deaths in 250 municipalities, 2010–2021. Hot spots in the north and centre, cold spots around Seoul.
  • Under 65 rates rose after 2017; rates at 65 and over fell from 82.12 to 42.19 per 100,000.
  • Mental health facilities (RR 0.945) and doctor density (0.975) were protective; single-person households (1.155) and stress (1.015) were risk factors.
R code · Spatial structure (neighbours + BYM graph)
nb <- poly2nb(map)
nb2INLA("map.adj", nb)
g <- inla.read.graph(filename = "map.adj")
su$idarea <- as.numeric(as.factor(su$SIG_NM))
su$SIG_CD1 <- su$SIG_CD
Results

Spatial setup

  • Queen contiguity neighbours → INLA graph
  • Used for all ages, under 65, and 65+ models
  • Global Moran’s I up to 0.21 (all ages), 0.299 (65+)
R code · BYM model – all ages
suicide_res <- inla(
  Suicide_counts ~ docpert + Highrisk_drinking + stress_percp +
    fin_indp + NDVI + Healthprom + Smoking + singleh +
    Depression + clinic + Sex_ratio +
    offset(log(Population1)) +
    f(idarea, model = "bym", graph = g) +
    f(SIG_CD1, Idtime, model = "iid") + Idtime,
  family = "nbinomial", data = su,
  control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE),
  control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE)
)
Results

All ages (BYM)

  • Mental health facilities RR 0.945
  • Doctor density 0.975 · MH specialists 0.964
  • Financial autonomy 0.957 (protective)
  • Single households 1.155 · Stress 1.015 (risk)
  • DIC 146,358
R code · BYM model – under 65
suicide_res <- inla(
  Under_65_cases ~ Find_ind + single_household + Current_smoking +
    Stress_perception + Health_prom_facilities + Depression +
    Doctors + Highrisk_drinking + NDVI + Mental_health_wf +
    Clinic + Sex_ratio + offset(log(Pop_under65)) +
    f(idarea, model = "bym", graph = g) +
    f(SIG_CD1, Idtime, model = "iid") + Idtime,
  family = "nbinomial", data = su,
  control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE)
)
Results

Under 65 (BYM)

  • Mental health facilities RR 0.954
  • MH specialists 0.963 · Financial autonomy 0.963
  • Single households 1.126 · Stress 1.018
  • Doctor density not significant in this age group
R code · BYM model – 65 and over
# Same BYM structure; outcome = deaths 65+
# offset(log(Pop_65plus))
suicide_res <- inla(
  cases_65plus ~ ... + offset(log(Pop_65plus)) +
    f(idarea, model = "bym", graph = g) +
    f(SIG_CD1, Idtime, model = "iid") + Idtime,
  family = "nbinomial", data = su,
  control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE)
)
Results

65 and over (BYM)

  • Doctor density RR 0.947 (protective)
  • Single households 1.036 · Stress 1.019
  • Mental health facilities / specialists not significant
R code · Relative risk extraction (example)
irrs <- inla.tmarginal(function(x) exp(x),
                       suicide_res$marginals.fixed$Stress_perception)
inla.qmarginal(c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975), irrs)
inla.emarginal(function(x) x, irrs)
# Repeat for each fixed effect (facilities, doctors, singleh, ...)
Results

RR transformation

  • Posterior marginals of coefficients → exp(·)
  • Reports median RR and 95% credible interval
  • Applied to every covariate in Tables 4–6

Analysis of monthly suicide deaths (ICD-10 X60–X84) in 250 municipalities (SiGunGu), run separately for all ages (age-standardised), under 65 and 65 and over. Methods: Global Moran’s I, Getis-Ord Gi* hot spots, Mann-Kendall trends, then Bayesian spatiotemporal negative binomial models (BYM, with ICAR as sensitivity analysis) fitted in R-INLA with log population as offset.

Global Moran’s I (Table 3)

Positive spatial autocorrelation was present in nearly every year; it was strongest in 2011 for all ages (0.21) and under 65 (0.199), and in 2013 for 65 and over (0.299). Under 65, 2013 (p = 0.063) and 2019 (p = 0.051) were not significant.

All ages (age-standardised)

Mortality fell gradually from 2010 to 2020 with a slight rise in 2021. Hot spots stayed mainly in the northern and central areas, with cold spots consistently in and around Seoul.

Under 65 years

Rates declined until 2017, then rose steadily, with spring and autumn seasonality. Hot spots were mainly northeastern and central, with Jeju-si and Seogwipo-si unique to 2020.

65 years and over

Mortality fell sharply, from 82.12 per 100,000 in 2010 to 42.19 in 2021, though this group still had the highest rates. Hot spots were mainly central and northern; cold spots were in the east and south, especially from 2013.

Only doctor density (RR 0.947) was protective. Single-person households (1.036) and stress (1.019) were risk factors, though the household estimate was not significant under ICAR.

Mann-Kendall trends by age and sex

Under 65, uptrends at 99% confidence appeared in parts of Chungbuk, Gyeonggi and Gyeongnam (males) and Seoul, Gyeonggi and Chungbuk (females). Among those 65 and over, downtrends were widespread.

Conclusion

Patterns over time and space

  • Suicide rates under 65 fell until 2017 and then rose, while rates at 65 and over fell from 82.12 to 42.19 per 100,000 between 2010 and 2021.
  • Spatial autocorrelation was positive in almost every year (Moran’s I up to 0.21 for all ages, 0.199 under 65, 0.299 at 65 and over). Under 65 it was not significant in 2013 and 2019.
  • Hot spots were mainly in the northern, central and northeastern areas, and cold spots were in and around Seoul.
  • Mann-Kendall tests showed significant uptrends under 65 in parts of Chungbuk, Gyeonggi, Gyeongnam, Daegu and Seoul, and widespread downtrends at 65 and over.

Significant factors in the Bayesian (BYM) models

  • All ages: lower suicide mortality with more mental health promotion facilities (RR 0.945), higher doctor density (0.975), more mental health specialists (0.964) and higher financial autonomy (0.957). Higher mortality with more single-person households (1.155) and stress perception (1.015).
  • Under 65: lower with mental health facilities (0.954), mental health specialists (0.963) and financial autonomy (0.963). Higher with single-person households (1.126) and stress (1.018).
  • 65 and over: lower with doctor density (0.947). Higher with single-person households (1.036) and stress (1.019).
  • Depression experience, smoking, high-risk drinking and NDVI were not significant in any group.
